stem: Imran sees a poster: Club P has $15$ members drawn as a wide bar, and Club Q has $45$ members drawn as a bar only a little wider than Club P's bar, not about three times as wide.

options.text: Do not trust the poster as an accurate representation, because the bar widths do not keep the $15$ to $45$ relationship.
Trust the poster, because Club Q's bar is still a little wider than Club P's bar.
The drawn bar widths produce the membership counts, so start from the artwork and invent the numbers $15$ and $45$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Club Q has three times as many members as Club P, so an accurate bar for Q should be about three times as wide; a bar that is only a little wider distorts the data.

teacher.key_rationale: Accurate visuals must preserve numerical relationships. A slightly wider bar for a triple count omits the scale condition. Starting from artwork to invent the counts reverses the data-to-display relation.
